topics.title: Meet the Guitar
topics.short: The parts of a guitar, from the headstock to the bridge, how the six strings are numbered, and the difference between steel-string, nylon-string and electric guitars.

topics.title: Holding the Guitar
topics.short: How to sit with a guitar, where each hand goes, how to press a string so it rings clearly, how to hold a pick, and how to look after your hands.

topics.title: Tuning Up
topics.short: How to tune a guitar to E A D G B E: with the microphone tuner, by ear with reference notes, and by the 5th-fret method, string against string.

topics.title: Reading Tab
topics.short: Guitar tablature: six lines for six strings, numbers for frets, how rhythm is shown under the tab, and how tab and standard notation fit together.

topics.title: Reading Chord Charts
topics.short: How to read a guitar chord diagram: strings and frets, dots and finger numbers, open and muted strings, barres and fret numbers.

topics.title: Your First Notes
topics.short: Picking single notes on the top three strings: the notes E, F, G on string 1, B, C, D on string 2 and G, A on string 3, with down strokes and alternate picking, and a first tune.

topics.title: First Chords: Em, Am, E and A
topics.short: Four easy chords that share the same finger shapes: E minor, A minor, E major and A major, how to make every string ring, and a first strum.

topics.title: G, C and D: the Campfire Chords
topics.short: The three chords behind thousands of folk, country and cowboy songs: G, C and D, plus D7 and G7, and how they belong together in the key of G.

topics.title: Strumming Patterns
topics.short: How to strum in time: down strums on the beat, down-up eighths, the folk strum with its missed stroke, and accents and muted chucks.

topics.title: Changing Chords in Time
topics.short: How to move from one chord to the next without stopping the beat: anchor fingers, moving all fingers together, letting go early, and one-minute changes.

topics.title: Bass and Strum: Waltz and Boom-Chuck
topics.short: The country and cowboy way to accompany a song: a bass note followed by a strum. The waltz in 3/4 and the boom-chuck with an alternating bass in 4/4.

topics.title: The Twelve-Bar Blues
topics.short: The twelve-bar blues in E: the chord pattern behind countless blues songs, the E7, A7 and B7 chords, the two-string shuffle and swing eighths.

topics.title: Notes on the Neck
topics.short: Finding every natural note in first position, sharps and flats on the fretboard, octaves, and how tab and standard notation show the same music.

topics.title: Fingerpicking: p, i, m, a
topics.short: Playing with the fingers instead of a pick: the thumb on the bass strings, index, middle and ring on the top strings, arpeggio patterns, and a first classical prelude.

topics.title: Two Parts at Once: Classical Guitar
topics.short: Playing a tune and a bass together, the way classical guitarists do: free strokes and rest strokes, letting notes ring, reading two voices, and pieces by Carulli and Sor.

topics.title: The F Chord and Barres
topics.short: The F chord in three steps, from a small four-string F to the full barre, B minor and B7, and how to make a barre ring without squeezing.

topics.title: Movable Chords Up the Neck
topics.short: Barre chords as movable shapes: the E shape with its root on string 6, the A shape with its root on string 5, minor and seventh versions, and power chords.

topics.title: Scales on the Guitar
topics.short: The C and G major scales in first position, the A minor pentatonic box at the 5th fret, the blues scale, and how scales help you play tunes and improvise.

topics.title: Hammer-Ons, Slides and Bends: Country Blues
topics.short: The left-hand tricks that make the blues talk: hammer-ons, pull-offs, slides and bends, and the steady-thumb fingerpicking of the early country blues.

topics.title: Travis Picking
topics.short: Alternating-thumb fingerpicking: the thumb swings between two bass strings on every beat while the index and middle fingers pick between them, with pinches and a melody on top.

topics.title: Spanish Sounds
topics.short: The sound of Spanish guitar: the Andalusian cadence (Am, G, F, E), the step from F to G-sharp, rest strokes, a first rasgueado, and the triplet arpeggio of the Spanish Romance.

topics.title: The Capo, Keys and Harmonics
topics.short: How a capo raises the open strings so the same chord shapes play in a new key, how to find the right capo fret for a singer, and natural harmonics at frets 12, 7 and 5.

topics.title: Practice and Next Steps
topics.short: How to practice guitar well in twenty minutes a day, looking after your hands and your strings, and where to go next with the songs on this site.
